title: CAR Algebras, Majorana Generators, and Clifford Comparison

items.title: Fermionic Fock Space over a Complex Hilbert Space
items.definition: For a complex Hilbert space H, the fermionic Fock space is the Hilbert completion of the orthogonal algebraic direct sum of its Hilbert exterior powers Λ^k H, k≥0; the vacuum is 1∈Λ^0 H.

items.title: Finite-Mode Complex CAR Algebra
items.definition: For n≥0, form the free unital complex *-algebra on a_j,a_j† (1≤j≤n), with adjoint reversing words and exchanging symbols. Quotient by the two-sided *-ideal generated by {a_i,a_j}=0, {a_i†,a_j†}=0, {a_i,a_j†}=δ_ij1.

items.title: Square-Summable Complex Families Form a Hilbert Space

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis, Chapter 1, sequence-space completeness
Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis, sequence-space completeness

items.statement: For every set I, the complex square-summable family space ℓ²(I,C) with its canonical norm and inner product is complete and hence Hilbert; finitely supported families are dense, and coordinate vectors form an orthonormal basis. The proof uses no choice principle.

items.title: Finite-Dimensional CAR Algebra over an Inner-Product Space
items.definition: For a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space F with inner product linear in its first variable, define the universal *-algebra generated complex-linearly by c(f), with {c(f),c(g)}=0, {c(f)*,c(g)*}=0, and {c(f)*,c(g)}=<g,f>1.

items.title: Finite CAR Occupation Operators Give All Matrix Units

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6, §§6.1–6.3
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, §§4.2 and 5.7

items.statement: On the Hilbert space with orthonormal basis e_S indexed by subsets S⊆{1,…,n}, the signed occupation toggles c_j,c_j† satisfy CAR and the operators c_{i_1}†…c_{i_p}† P_∅ c_{j_q}…c_{j_1} are all matrix units.

items.title: Fock Creation and Annihilation Operators Satisfy the CAR

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6 §§6.1 and 6.7
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations §§4.1 and 5.7

items.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, wedge creation C(f) on fermionic Fock space is bounded with norm ||f||, its adjoint A(f) satisfies {C(f),C(g)}={A(f),A(g)}=0 and {A(f),C(g)}=<g,f>I.

items.title: Finite-Mode CAR and the Complex Clifford Algebra via Majorana Generators

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6, §§6.1–6.4
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, §§4.1–4.2

items.statement: For V=C^{2n} with Q(Σz_re_r)=Σz_r², γ_{2j−1}=a_j+a_j† and γ_{2j}=i(a_j†−a_j) induce inverse *-isomorphisms between the plus-Q complex Clifford algebra and the finite-mode CAR algebra.

items.title: The Finite-Mode CAR Algebra Is a Full Matrix Algebra

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6, §§6.2–6.5
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, §§4.1–4.2

items.statement: For n≥0, CAR_n is *-isomorphic to M_{2^n}(C); its universal C*-norm is the standard matrix operator norm.

items.title: Canonical Finite-Mode CAR Inclusions Are Isometric

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6, §6.4
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, §4.2

items.statement: The canonical map CAR_n→CAR_{n+1} that fixes the first n modes is isometric and injective; in the occupation model it is A↦A⊗I_2.

items.title: Finite-Dimensional CAR over an Inner-Product Space Is a Matrix Algebra

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6 §§6.2–6.4
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations §§4.1–4.2

items.statement: For every finite-dimensional complex inner-product space F of dimension n, CAR(F) is *-isomorphic to M_(2^n)(C), has its unique finite-dimensional universal C*-norm, and every unital *-representation on a nonzero Hilbert space is isometric.

items.title: Countably Infinite-Mode CAR C*-Algebra
items.definition: The countably infinite-mode CAR C*-algebra is the norm completion of the increasing union of the finite-mode universal CAR C*-algebras under the canonical isometric inclusions a_j↦a_j.

items.title: Finite-Subspace CAR Inclusions Are Isometric

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6 §6.4
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations §4.2

items.statement: For finite-dimensional subspaces F⊆G of a complex Hilbert space, the generator-preserving CAR(F)→CAR(G) map extends to an isometric unital *-homomorphism of their matrix C*-completions.

items.title: CAR C*-Algebra over a Complex Hilbert Space
items.definition: For a complex Hilbert space H, take the directed union of the finite-dimensional CAR(F) C*-algebras over all finite-dimensional subspaces F⊂H under their isometric generator-preserving inclusions, and complete it in the common stage norm.

items.title: Particle-Hole Exchange Is an Automorphism of Countable-Mode CAR

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6, §§6.4 and 6.7
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, §4.1

items.statement: The map a_j↦a_j†, a_j†↦a_j extends to an involutive *-automorphism of CAR_N.

items.title: The Countable CAR Algebra Has the Universal Inductive-Limit Norm

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6, §§6.1 and 6.4
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, §§4.1 and 5.7

items.statement: Every countable bounded CAR family with its specified Hilbert adjoints extends uniquely and contractively to CAR_N, and the inductive-limit norm is the supremum over all such representations. The occupation-space coordinate vectors form an orthonormal basis, with finite-support span dense.

items.title: The Countable-Mode CAR Fock Representation Is Irreducible

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6, §§6.1 and 6.7
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, §5.7

items.statement: The occupation representation on ℓ² of finite subsets of N is irreducible; its common annihilator kernel is the vacuum line and its common creator kernel is zero.

items.title: CAR over a Hilbert Space Has the Universal Inductive-Limit Norm

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6 §§6.4 and 6.7
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations §§4.1, 4.2 and 5.7

items.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, every nonzero-Hilbert-space representation of the CAR over a complex Hilbert space H extends uniquely and isometrically to CAR(H); the inductive-limit norm is the supremum of represented norms, witnessed by fermionic Fock space.

items.title: Countable-Mode CAR Has Inequivalent Irreducible Representations

references.title: Günther Hörmann, C*-Algebras with Aspects of Quantum Physics, Chapter 6, §6.7
Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, §§4.1 and 5.7

items.statement: The Fock representation and its composition with the particle-hole automorphism are inequivalent irreducible representations of CAR_N; no classification of all irreducibles is asserted.

title: CAR Algebras, Majorana Generators, and Clifford Comparison: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: One-Mode CAR and Its Two Majorana Matrices
items.statement: For one mode, a=[[0,1],[0,0]] and a†=[[0,0],[1,0]] satisfy CAR; the two Majorana generators are the Pauli matrices σ_x and σ_y.

items.title: Two-Mode CAR Signs and a Matrix Unit
items.statement: The two-mode occupation matrices exhibit the fermionic minus sign and the matrix unit E_{1,2}=a_1†P_∅a_2.

items.title: The Countable-Mode CAR Algebra Has a Non-Fock-Equivalent Irreducible Representation
items.statement: The claim that every irreducible countable-mode CAR representation is unitarily equivalent to Fock is false: the particle-hole-twisted Fock representation is irreducible and inequivalent.
